key_insight: Targeted neural networks can learn self-shielded microscopic cross sections for multigroup reactor calculations using only fuel nuclide concentrations as inputs.
engineering_relevance: This could reduce the manual effort and expert tuning needed to generate multigroup nuclear data libraries for light water reactor analysis.
method: Trained artificial neural networks on 8,704 OpenMC pincell samples generated with continuous-energy transport.
Predicted self-shielded total, fission, absorption, elastic, and scattering cross sections for 90 nuclides in the CASMO-8 group structure.
Validated against 1,500 unseen reference samples and then used the predicted data in multigroup eigenvalue calculations.
evidence_signal: On unseen test data, predicted and reference cross sections agreed to within 0.119% on average, and keff error in multigroup runs averaged 200 pcm.
watch_item: The model is demonstrated for a fixed pincell geometry and temperature, so broader reactor conditions may require retraining or additional generalization checks.
paper_title: Self-Shielded Multigroup Microscopic Cross Section Generation Using Targeted Artificial Neural Networks
